messages:
raj: :rotating_light: Customer ACME reports PII surfaced in audit logs after failover; they say requests ended up in us-west despite EU pin. ticket: https://support.example.com/t/3421 — says 500s then ok but residency flag tripped. Can someone triage?
emma: looking — any repro steps or sample request ids?
raj: pasted request id and headers in the ticket: req=abc123, X-Geo: eu, Authorization session=acct-55, customer says latency spiked ~2s then 500s for a minute.
sophia: pulling audit logs for req=abc123 now. quick grep shows: 
```
{"ts":"1700007889","req":"abc123","route":"fallback","dest_region":"us-west-2","residency_violation":true,"policy":"eu_only","kms_action":"DENY"}
```
leo: interesting — KMS deny but data still routed then failed? that log shows dest_region was us-west-2 but kms denied write — maybe we retried to fallback pool.
maria: customer claims billing spike for that interval — they saw higher token usage and a few retries. can billing team confirm duplicate charges?
emma: I'm hypothesizing: primary EU pool was degraded, router triggered a fallback policy that should be soft-blocked for eu_only customers but a bug in policy-eval allowed passthrough then KMS denied at write causing 500s. need to confirm policy decision path and router decision reason.
sophia: grabbing router decision trace for that time window. route-decide logs show: 
```
[router] req=abc123 user=acct-55 policy_check=ERROR timeout=30ms fallback_allowed=true selected_pool=pool-fallback-us-west
```
incident-bot: New compliance alert created: CL-2024-662 for account acct-55 (eu_only policy breach)
leo: can we repro in staging by simulating eu pool slow + fallback? if yes we can test patch.
emma: yes will reproduce. quick checklist: 1) pin user acct-55 policy eu_only in env 2) throttle eu pool to mimic latencies 3) ensure fallback pool marked as incompatible — expect router to reject. If router selects fallback that’s the bug.
maria: I've opened billing ticket BT-901 and flagged for potential credit if duplicate billing confirmed.
sophia: tracing shows a race: policy-eval RPC timed out -> defaulted to previous policy state which had fallback_allowed=true. root cause could be a timeout threshold too low.
raj: customer wants explanation and an SLA credit. also compliance needs audit entries corrected.
emma: immediate mitigations: 1) raise policy-eval timeout to 200ms on router cluster (hotfix) 2) push a temporary block rule for eu_only customers to prevent cross-region routing 3) notify customer and schedule postmortem. I'll deploy hotfix to canary in eu and monitor.
leo: i'll craft a short incident banner for console: "Investigating region routing for some EU customers; temporary protective rule applied."
maria: i'll coordinate billing outreach and pre-draft credit proposal.
sophia: follow-up: saving the relevant logs and adding to CL-2024-662. we'll need to scrub logs for PII before sharing.
emma: assigned follow-ups: emma (hotfix + canary), sophia (trace + postmortem), leo (customer comm + console banner), maria (billing). ETA for initial customer update: 45m.
raj: thanks all. keep thread updated. :shield:
